drafts.angle: Mirror-list aphorism (rides @AlexHormozi's 'top 1% in money... top 1% in stress', 135K and 1.1K bookmarks)
drafts.draft_en:
The teams shipping 1,000 AI ad variants a week also have 1,000 chances a week to break a brand rule, a legal claim, or a platform policy.

If you want the first number, you need a check for the second.
drafts.video_tip: 12s vertical, text-only. Line 1 counts up '1,000 variants' in green, line 2 counts up '1,000 chances to break a rule' in red, then hold the last sentence for 3 seconds. No logo until the final frame.

drafts.angle: AI-pilled playbook (rides @gregisenberg's 'Making the most AI pilled company is the whole game', 82K and 3.9K bookmarks)
drafts.draft_en:
Making the most AI-pilled marketing team is the whole game:

1. Put your brand rules in one folder of markdown files a machine can read

2. Write down your legal no-go claims, not just your voice and tone

3. Let agents make as many ad variants as you want

4. Check every single one before it ships: approve, fix, or block

5. Spend your time on the ones that passed
drafts.video_tip: 30s screen recording: open a folder of brand-rule markdown files, drop in a batch of AI ad variants, and show each one getting an APPROVE, FIX, or BLOCK badge in Aubric. Voiceover reads the 5 steps. Use only real product footage.

drafts.angle: Eval verdict in line one (rides @garrytan's 'Keep Opus 5.5 as your coding default' and harness eval repo, 357 bookmarks)
drafts.draft_en:
When you pick a model to review ads, don't pick it from a leaderboard.

Pick it by cost per correct verdict on your own creative: the bad claims, off-brand colors, and policy edge cases your team actually ships.

That's how we're choosing models for Aubric's checks.
drafts.video_tip: 20s vertical: a simple table with model names down the side and 'cost per correct verdict' across the top, filled in row by row. Only use numbers from an eval you actually ran; if you haven't run one yet, post this as text only.
